notes: THE FIRST RECORD IN THIS REPO TO DECLARE ITS OWN NON-INDEPENDENCE. The reviewer was asked twice to set this field honestly and twice refused to claim independence it cannot establish, declaring true rather than a purity neither party can demonstrate. That is the field working as designed, on its first use, against the mechanism's own author. Three passes, the first of which defeated this PR entirely. PASS 1 (bd6a681) found the load-bearing bypass: the cutoff gated every new check -- identity format, token collision, the required declaration -- on data.get('pr'), a field inside the record itself, never reconciled against the directory it sits in. The reviewer wrote reviews/19/sneaky.json declaring 'pr': 18 with free-form ids and no declaration, and it passed with zero errors and zero notices, fully satisfying the shared-path gate. A string '19' bypassed identically because the hand-rolled schema validator checked required, enum and pattern but never type. Worse, the comment I wrote for that cutoff cited scripts/lwb_check_proof.py's identical unchecked-pr pattern as PRECEDENT, so I propagated a known hole rather than closing the class. It also found that the identity format could not express lw-verifier or claude-sonnet-5, since any hyphen in role or model failed the regex -- pushing authors to degrade their own identifiers to satisfy a validator, the same falsification pressure this PR claims to reduce, relocated to id construction. PASS 2 (29e11b1) confirmed the bypass closed against a wider battery than requested -- pr absent, 19.0, True with isinstance(True, int) excluded, -5, a nested path, a symlink to another PR's record, a non-canonical reviews/019/ directory -- and verified independently that lwb_check_proof.py's self-declared pr IS reconciled against github.event.pull_request.number on one path and the squash-merge subject on the other, so the class really was closed rather than moved. It then found that parsing from the right and comparing the segment adjacent to the date broke in BOTH directions: an author could shift what gets compared by appending one segment, defeating the collision check entirely, while two unrelated ids sharing a coincidental trailing chunk were wrongly rejected. And the finding that settles the design: in the REAL records for PRs 15, 16 and 17 the shared token f8da3f9e is NOT adjacent to the date -- it sits before a scope field -- so the positional rule would have missed the exact three records that motivated building the mechanism. PASS 3, this record, on 47ba623: both halves fixed by comparing the two ids as sets of hyphen-delimited segments with the trailing date excluded, flagging any shared segment of at least eight characters. Verified against the ten real records rather than synthetic ones: 15, 16 and 17 flagged on f8da3f9e, 7 through 13 and 18 clean. The reviewer probed _id_segments for crashes across consecutive hyphens, trailing hyphens, empty segments, a bare date, a missing date suffix, a malformed year and unicode segments -- none raises. RESIDUAL, recorded in the code and README rather than resolved: a shared token shorter than eight characters goes undetected, and this is not hypothetical, since reviews/schema.json accepts a seven-character git short sha as a legitimate identifier and a UUID's later groups are four characters. No floor value closes both that and the false-positive problem. CORRECTION THE REVIEWER FORCED: my commit message called the lengthened four-character collision test the fifth vacuous test in this repo. It ran it -- against the current code that test fails loudly, it was never vacuous. The lengthening was right, my characterisation was not, and it is corrected in the commit that follows. What this buys is that an honest one must consciously declare the relationship and watch the gate announce it. REBOUND: this record first named 47ba623.
